content.title: ORGAN-FOOD PAIRS NUTRITIONISTS ACTUALLY USE THEMSELVES
facts: **Beef heart** is good for YOUR HEART – it's one of the richest natural sources of CoQ10, a compound your own heart muscle burns for energy.
**Brazil nuts (2/day)** are good for THYROID – just two nuts cover your daily selenium, a mineral your thyroid needs to make its hormones.
**Beetroot greens** are good for EYES – the leafy tops carry more lutein than the root itself, a pigment your retina stores directly.
**Octopus and clams** are good for BLOOD – they're loaded with iron and B12, both needed to build fresh red blood cells.
**Cacao nibs (1 tbsp/day)** are good for ARTERIES – the flavanols help keep vessel walls flexible so blood pressure stays steadier.
**Bone broth** is good for JOINTS – it supplies collagen fragments your cartilage uses as raw building material.
**Turmeric with black pepper** is good for LIVER – piperine in the pepper helps your body actually absorb turmeric's active compound.
**Pistachios (small handful)** are good for LUNGS – they're one of the few nuts with notable potassium, which helps regulate airway function.
**Anchovies** are good for BONES – tiny bones and all, they hand you calcium and vitamin D in the same bite.
**Follow along** – for more daily health tips like this.

caption:
A few of these deserve a closer look. Beef heart isn't something most people reach for, but it's genuinely one of the densest food sources of CoQ10 — a compound your heart cells use to generate the energy needed for every single beat. Brazil nuts work differently: your thyroid can't produce T3 and T4 hormones without enough selenium, and most people are quietly running low without realizing it. And bone broth isn't just a trend — the collagen peptides in it get broken down and used as literal building blocks for the cartilage cushioning your joints. Everyone's body is different, so start with one swap and see how you feel.
